approach: Two changes at the source. (1) Reclaim: in disk.rs add `sweep_interrupted_targets` and `Athena::reclaim_interrupted`. They remove only `target/` of jobs that are Dispatched in Records, have no registry entry after `reap()`, are not on a keep list, and whose job lock `try_lock_job` can take (held while removing). In drain.rs add a defaulted `Steps::reclaim_interrupted(own: &[String])`, called once at drain start (before `steps.queue()`) and in `run_job` before `steps.run`, with the drain's own jobs as the keep list; `RealSteps` forwards to the Athena method. (2) Pre-producer gate: in producer.rs add `producer_disk_gate` (one call of the existing `disk_gate`), called from `produce_and_verify` in run/mod.rs right after `baseline_stage` and before the work tree and snapshot exist. On low space it returns `Err(self.hold_for_disk(ctx, closing, low))`, the same hold the checks gate uses: records committed with no outcome, a hold marker, `go` returns LowDisk, no attempt used. All new behavior tests go in the existing integration file crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (which already imports athena_cli and Fixture). There is no `#[path]` include and no stub Job record: interrupted jobs are made with the existing `request_on` + `interrupt` (real ask/go with a killed producer). One small disk.rs unit test covers the lock and keep-list logic of the sweep on a bare StateDir.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 2: add the pre-producer gate now, no question to the user. `Athena::producer_disk_gate` in run/producer.rs wraps `disk_gate(jc.config.min_free_gb(), id, ui)`. `produce_and_verify` (run/mod.rs) calls it after `baseline_stage` and before `job_worktree`/`producer_snapshot`, and on low space returns `Err(self.hold_for_disk(ctx, closing, low))`.
decisions.reason: Root-cause default and the brief's deliverables list producer.rs and run/mod.rs. After the baseline checks (which build and are what fill the disk) and before the producer, nothing checked space; the dispatch gate (run/mod.rs:749) runs earlier. `produce_and_verify` owns `closing` by value, which `hold_for_disk` (close.rs:176) takes, and the Err flows through `finish_dispatched` the same way the check-gate hold at run/mod.rs:1303 does. The work tree does not exist yet, so nothing needs cleanup. The gate sweeps idle targets first and keeps the job's own, like the other gates.

rejected.option: Gate at the top of `producer_loop`'s pass (covers send-back reruns)
rejected.why: `producer_loop` holds `&mut Closing` while `hold_for_disk` needs it by value; fixing that means a new Flow variant or editing close.rs, outside the deliverables. A send-back rerun follows a producer that already ran, and the gate before the checks (run/mod.rs:1301) still covers its built candidate. Named as a risk.
Baseline is recorded only and never stops a job; the producer is the thing to protect, and the baseline's own build is what lowers space just before it.
`enter` returns `()`, so it cannot hold a job.
Repeats the dispatch gate a few lines before `go` and does not cover `athena go` outside drain.

decisions.choice: Reclaim `target/` only, via `StateDir::remove_target`, for jobs Dispatched in Records with no registry entry (after `registry().reap()`) not on the keep list and whose `try_lock_job` succeeds. Check the cheap predicates first, then the lock, so closed jobs get no lock file. `Athena::reclaim_interrupted` loads Records once; a failed head or load prints a `warning:` line and returns 0.
decisions.reason: The brief keeps work trees and candidates. status.rs:1615-1616 already calls Dispatched-and-not-running 'interrupted'. `go_job` takes the job lock before the Dispatched commit, so the lock covers the window the registry misses.

rejected.why: Filtered to drained channels and drops jobs a retry already names; some interrupted directories would stay.
Deletes the work tree; out of scope.
Misses the gap between the Dispatched commit and the first process spawn.

rejected.option: Sweep every unlocked dir like sweep_idle_targets
rejected.why: That rule runs only once disk is already low; the fault is that nothing reclaims earlier.

decisions.choice: The keep list is the drain's own jobs: `reclaim_interrupted(&[])` at drain start; in `run_job` the item's job plus every id in `d.st().tried`. The sweep never takes their locks. The per-job remove body of `sweep_idle_targets` is factored into a private helper shared with the new sweep (behavior of the old one unchanged).
decisions.reason: `go_job` bails with 'already running' if the lock is taken (run/mod.rs:308-310); a sweep holding a worker's lock could make its `go` fail. The drain retries an interrupted item as a new job id, so it never needs the interrupted id's lock. One remaining race (an outside `athena retry X` during the sweep of X) is a named risk.

rejected.why: Does not protect other workers in a concurrent drain.

rejected.option: Probe the lock without holding it
rejected.why: The remove could overlap a job that just started building.

decisions.reason: Existing tests assert the exact `stub.log()`; a new log entry would break them. The Stub only records calls; the when-to-call logic is production drain code. The Records/registry/lock rule runs for real.

risks.risk: The sweep removes a live job's build directory, or holds a lock a starting job needs.
risks.mitigation: Requires Dispatched in Records, no registry entry after `reap()`, a lock `try_lock_job` can take, and a job outside the keep list. The lock covers the window before any process is registered. The guard test covers lock, registry, closed and keep cases.

risks.risk: An outside `athena retry X` or `athena go X` on an interrupted X while the sweep holds X's lock fails with 'already running in another athena process'.
risks.mitigation: The drain's own jobs are never swept, so its workers cannot hit it. The lock is held only while one `target/` is removed. A rerun succeeds. Named in the CHANGELOG and docs.

risks.risk: The new pre-producer gate holds a job that previously ran, when free space is between the old checks' thresholds.
risks.mitigation: It uses the same `min_free_gb` and sweeps idle targets first, as the dispatch and check gates do, so it only holds when those would soon hold too; the default is unchanged. The hold is an environment stop with no attempt used, and a later drain retries the job.

risks.risk: A job held before the producer is Dispatched with no resume mark; the next drain retries it as a new job from the base.
risks.mitigation: That is how any interrupted job without a candidate is resumed (retry reads it again). No work is lost since no candidate exists; the hold marker is cleared when the retry dispatches.

risks.risk: A resumed interrupted job loses a build cache it could reuse.
risks.mitigation: Only `target/` is removed; the criterion 1 test asserts the work tree and kept work remain.

risks.risk: A Records read at drain start and before each run stalls or aborts the drain.
risks.mitigation: One load per sweep; an unreadable head or records prints a `warning:` line and returns 0 bytes. It never fails the drain.

risks.risk: The new trait method breaks existing `Steps` implementors; the Stub's new field breaks exact-log assertions.
risks.mitigation: A default no-op body keeps implementors compiling; the Stub records calls in a separate field, not in `log`. Step 12 runs the whole workspace checks.

risks.risk: Existing run tests that count free-space reads or hold at the check gate change behavior with the new gate.
risks.mitigation: `built_then_low_disk` sets low space in the producer's script, after the new gate, so it still holds at the check gate (producer count 1). Step 12 runs all of them; the producer adjusts any assertion that relied on a read count.

demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain the_reclaim_keeps_live_locked_closed_and_own_jobs && cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain drain_reclaims_at_start_and_before_each_run && cargo test -p athena-core the_interrupted_sweep_skips_locked_and_kept_jobs
demonstrations.observes: (a) Four jobs made interrupted with `request_on` + `interrupt`, each with planted `target/` and `work/`: A no process; B with a live `sleep 60` child (`std::process::Command` + `process_group(0)`, `athena.state.registry().register(pgid, B, "test")`, kill-and-wait guard); C with its lock held by `athena.state.try_lock_job`; E on the keep list; plus a Proposed job closed with `athena.close(..)` that has a `target/` (D). `athena.reclaim_interrupted(&[E], &lines)` removes only A's `target/`; B, C, D and E keep theirs; every `work/` stays; a second call with the lock released and B's child killed (registry reaped) now removes B and C. A new job interrupted after the first sweep is removed by the next sweep (the later-run case). (b) The Stub records `(runs_so_far, own)` for each `reclaim_interrupted` call: one call with `[]` before `queue()` is consulted, and a call before each `run` whose `own` has that item's job and the earlier tried ones. (c) bare StateDir: locked and keep-listed jobs keep `target/`, the others lose it, `work/` stays.
demonstrations.fails_without: Ignoring the registry removes B's target; ignoring the lock removes C's; filtering on closed instead of Dispatched removes D's and keeps A's; ignoring the keep list removes E's. A drain that reclaims only at start gives (b) one call, not one per run; dropping the `run_job` call does the same.

demonstrations.method: Integration test through `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` and the production dispatch and producer path; space is low only after dispatch.
demonstrations.observes: Setup: `disk_fixture()` (10 GB required), a Script counting `Role::Producer` calls in an `Arc<AtomicUsize>`, `athena.state.with_free_space(simulated_free)` with no `simulated_free` file (plenty), `queue_steward_request`, and a `Ui` wrapper over `Lines` that writes 3_000_000_000 into `<state>/simulated_free` on the first line starting `baseline`. Run `drain(&RealSteps{ui: &wrapper, ..}, work_everything(), &Quiet)`. Asserts: the item's outcome is `environment: low disk`, the display text has `3.0 GB` and `10.0 GB`, `failed_item` is None, nothing landed; the producer counter is 0; Records show the job Dispatched with a job record, no outcome, no score (so it passed the dispatch gate; a dispatch-gate hold would leave it Proposed with no job record); `ui` lines are ordered `dispatched`, `baseline`, then `held       environment: low disk`; `disk::read_hold` gives 3 GB / 10 GB; `display::status(&athena.status().unwrap())` contains `interrupted`-state hold text `environment: low disk: 3.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required`; no line tells anyone to `athena retry`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `producer_disk_gate` the producer runs (counter is 1) and the job is held only later by the check gate, so the counter assert fails. If the hold were counted as a failure or committed an outcome, the outcome and Records asserts fail.
